correctness.rationale: The simple constrained eigenvalue defines an analytic inverse-penalty branch through the Schur-complement determinant. Standard symmetric perturbation yields the displayed first two coefficients; Hellmann–Feynman converts each computed eigenpair into derivative data, and the classical Hermite remainder gives O(rho^(-2q)). The explicit two-level formula cancels powers through rho^(-3), and the public numerical example exhibits a nonzero rho^(-4) leading error.

originality.rationale: The motivating source already supplies exact penalty duality, finite-recovery characterization, the first-order coefficient, a two-level value-only O(rho^-2) correction, and a one-level Hellmann–Feynman O(rho^-2) correction; these are not claimed. Classical Hermite/Richardson theory is also prior. The claim is restricted to the analytic simple-branch formulation, explicit second coefficient, q-level Hermite–Hellmann–Feynman O(rho^(-2q)) construction, closed two-level fourth-order formula, and coefficient-blind linear polynomial-exactness characterization. Searches found no overlapping SCOPE record or accessible external statement; older structural penalty literature and contemporaneous follow-up remain residual risks.

value.rationale: The result uses derivative information available from penalized eigenpairs to double inverse-power extrapolation order per penalty level. With two penalty solves it upgrades the generic value-only second-order scalar correction to fourth order, reducing the asymptotic penalty magnitude required for a target scalar error when the surviving coefficient is nonzero, without adding another eigenpair solve.
